title: A Day in My Life
text:
My name is Daniel, and I am a 17-year-old student. I usually wake up at 7 o'clock in the morning. First, I take a shower and get dressed. Then, I have breakfast with my family. I usually eat eggs and bread and drink a cup of tea.

I go to school at 8 o'clock. My lessons start at 8:30 and finish at 2 p.m. My favourite subjects are English and history because I enjoy learning new things. During the break, I talk to my classmates and sometimes play games with them.

After school, I come home and have lunch. Then, I do my homework and help my parents with some housework. In the evening, I sometimes watch movies, listen to music or go for a walk with my friends.

I usually have dinner at 8 p.m. After dinner, I spend some time with my family. Before going to bed, I read a book or watch a few videos. I usually go to bed at 10:30.

I like my daily routine because I have enough time for studying, relaxing and spending time with people I love.

title: My Family
text:
There are five people in our family: my parents, my two brothers and me. We live in a flat on the fourth floor of a tall building.

My father, Michael, works at a bank. He is a calm and patient man. He leaves home early, but he always comes back for dinner. My mother, Helen, is a nurse. She works long hours, but she is never too tired to listen to us.

Jack is my older brother. He is twenty and studies at university in another city, so we only see him at the weekends. Sam is my younger brother. He is only eight, and he is very funny and full of energy.

We are a close family. We get along well, but sometimes Sam and I argue about the TV! Every Sunday, we have a big lunch together at my grandparents' house. My grandmother cooks delicious soup, and my grandfather tells us stories about his childhood.

I love my family because they always support me, and I know I can talk to them about anything.

title: My Dream House
text:
Close your eyes and imagine your perfect home. Here is mine.

My dream house is not in a busy city. It is near a quiet lake, with mountains behind it. The house has two floors and big windows, so there is a lot of light in every room.

On the ground floor, there is a spacious living room with a fireplace and a comfortable sofa. Next to it, there is a modern kitchen. I want a big table there because I love cooking for my friends.

Upstairs, there are three bedrooms and two bathrooms. My bedroom has a balcony with a view of the lake. Every morning, I want to drink my tea there and watch the sunrise.

Outside, there is a large garden with fruit trees and flowers. I also want a small vegetable garden, like my grandmother has. In the corner of the garden, there is a little wooden house for my dog.

Of course, a house like this is expensive. But I am saving money every month, and one day I hope to build it.

title: Traditional Food Around the World
text:
Every country has its own traditional food. These dishes tell us a lot about the people and their history.

In Italy, people love pasta and pizza. Real Italian pizza is thin, and it is often cooked in a hot stone oven. Families in Italy usually eat lunch together, and a meal can last two hours.

In Japan, rice is part of almost every meal. People also eat a lot of fish and vegetables. Sushi is the most famous Japanese dish. It is made with rice, raw fish and seaweed.

Mexico is famous for tacos. A taco is a soft or crispy tortilla with meat, beans, cheese and spicy sauce. Many Mexicans eat tacos for breakfast, lunch and dinner!

In India, many dishes are full of spices. Curry is very popular, and people often eat it with rice or flat bread. In the south of India, some people eat with their right hand.

In Britain, a traditional breakfast has eggs, sausages, beans and toast. It is called a full English breakfast, and it is very filling.

Trying traditional food is one of the best ways to learn about a new culture.

title: How People Spend Their Free Time
text:
What do people do when they are not working or studying? Last month, our English class asked 50 people this question. Here are the results.

The most popular free-time activity is watching videos and films. Thirty people said they watch something every evening, usually on their phones. Many of them also listen to music while they travel to work or school.

Sports are popular too. Twelve people go to the gym or play football at least twice a week. Older people prefer walking in the park. They say it helps them relax after a busy day.

Some people like quiet hobbies. Eight people read books, and five people enjoy cooking new recipes at the weekend. One woman told us she paints pictures of flowers in her free time.

Young people spend a lot of time with friends. They meet in cafés, play computer games together or chat online for hours.

The survey shows one important thing: everyone needs free time. It helps people feel happy, healthy and full of energy.

title: A True Friendship
text:
When Tom was ten, his family moved to a new town. On his first day at the new school, he felt nervous and lonely. Nobody talked to him during the break.

Then a boy with curly hair sat next to him. "Hi, I'm Ben," he said. "Do you want to play football with us?" Tom smiled. From that day, they became best friends.

Tom and Ben did everything together. They walked to school, did their homework and watched football matches on TV. Ben was always cheerful, and Tom was good at maths, so they helped each other.

When they were fifteen, Tom broke his leg while he was playing football. He stayed at home for six weeks. Every day after school, Ben visited him. He brought Tom's homework and told him all the school news. Tom never felt bored or alone.

Now Tom and Ben are twenty-five. They live in different cities, but they still call each other every week. Tom often says, "A true friend is someone who stays with you on good days and bad days."

title: A Day at School
text:
Last Friday was a special day at Greenfield School: it was Science Day.

Lucy arrived at school at eight o'clock, earlier than usual. The school hall was full of tables, posters and strange machines. Every class had a project. Lucy's class made a small model of a volcano.

The first lesson was maths, but nobody could think about numbers. Everybody was excited. At ten o'clock, the bell rang, and the visitors came in: parents, teachers from other schools and a real scientist from the local university.

Lucy and her classmates stood next to their volcano. When the scientist came to their table, Lucy explained how a volcano works. Then her friend Max poured vinegar into the model. Red foam came out of the top, and everyone laughed and clapped.

At lunchtime, the students ate pizza in the playground. In the afternoon, the head teacher gave prizes. Lucy's class won second prize! Each student got a certificate and a science book.

On the way home, Lucy said to her mum, "That was the best school day of the year!"

title: The Benefits of Having a Hobby
text:
A hobby is something you do in your free time because you enjoy it. Some people collect stamps, some play the guitar, and others grow plants. But did you know that hobbies are also good for us?

First, hobbies help us reduce stress. When you are busy with something you love, you forget about your problems for a while. For example, many people say that drawing or gardening makes them feel calm.

Second, hobbies help us learn new skills. A person who plays chess learns to think carefully. Someone who cooks learns to plan and to be creative. These skills are useful at school and at work too.

Third, hobbies help us make friends. When you join a club or a team, you meet people with the same interests. Emma, a 16-year-old student, joined a photography club last year. "Now I have five new friends," she says, "and we go out to take photos every Saturday."

Finally, hobbies make life more interesting. So if you don't have a hobby yet, why not try something new this month?

title: A Shopping Day
text:
Last Saturday, Anna and her mum went shopping because Anna needed new clothes for school.

They took the bus to the biggest shopping centre in the city. It was very crowded, so they made a plan. First, they went to a clothes shop on the second floor. Anna found a pair of dark blue jeans and a white shirt. She tried them on in the changing room. The jeans were too long, so the shop assistant brought her a smaller size. This time, they fit perfectly.

Next, they needed shoes. Anna liked a pair of black trainers, but they cost eighty pounds. "That's too expensive," said her mum. Luckily, there was a sale in another shop, and they bought similar trainers for forty pounds.

By two o'clock, they were tired and hungry. They had lunch in a small café on the top floor. Anna had a chicken sandwich and an orange juice.

Before going home, they stopped at the supermarket and bought food for the week. Anna's mum paid by card. It was a long but happy day.

title: My Hometown
text:
I was born in Brookfield, a small town by a river in the north of England, and I have lived here all my life.

About twenty thousand people live in Brookfield. It is not famous, but it is a lovely place. The town centre has a market square, an old church and a lot of small shops and cafés. Every Thursday, farmers from nearby villages come to the market and sell fresh fruit, vegetables and cheese.

My favourite place is the park next to the river. In summer, people have picnics there, and children swim in the river. In winter, it is very quiet, and I like walking there with my dog.

Brookfield has two schools, a hospital and a small library. The library is my second favourite place. I often go there after school to read or study.

Of course, my town is not perfect. There is no cinema, so we have to take the train to a bigger city to watch new films. And there isn't much to do in the evenings.

Still, I love my hometown. People are friendly, and everyone knows everyone.

title: My First Big Trip
text:
Two years ago, I travelled abroad for the first time. My aunt invited me to visit her in Edinburgh, Scotland, for ten days during the summer holidays.

The journey was an adventure. My flight left at six in the morning, so I woke up at three. I was nervous because I was travelling alone, but a friendly flight attendant helped me find my seat. When the plane landed, my aunt was waiting for me at the airport with a big smile.

Edinburgh is an old and beautiful city. On my first day, we climbed the hill to Edinburgh Castle. From the top, we could see the whole city and the sea. The next day, we visited a museum and walked along the Royal Mile, the most famous street in the old town.

The weather surprised me. It was July, but it was cold and windy, and it rained almost every afternoon. I had to buy a warm jacket!

The trip changed me. I became more confident, and I discovered that I love exploring new places. Next year, I am planning to visit my aunt again.

title: My Dreams for the Future
text:
Everyone has dreams. Some dreams are small, and some are very big. Here are the dreams of three teenagers.

Sara is sixteen and loves animals. She wants to become a vet. "Right now, I'm studying biology and chemistry very hard," she says. "After school, I'm going to apply to a university in London." Sara also volunteers at an animal shelter every Saturday. She feeds the dogs and cleans their cages.

Oliver, seventeen, has a different dream. He wants to start his own business. Last year, he started selling handmade phone cases online, and he already has more than two hundred customers. "In ten years, I hope to have a small company with ten workers," he explains.

Mia is fifteen. Her dream is to travel around the world and write about it. She keeps a diary and writes something in it every day. She is also learning Spanish and French. "I want to visit at least thirty countries," she says with a smile.

Their dreams are different, but they have one thing in common: they are all working hard today to make their dreams come true tomorrow.

title: Different Jobs Around Us
text:
Every day, many people work to make our lives easier. We don't always notice them, but we need them.

Early in the morning, before most people wake up, bakers are already working. They start at four o'clock and make fresh bread for shops and cafés. At the same time, bus drivers get ready to take people to work and school.

Doctors and nurses work in hospitals day and night. Their job is very important, but it is also stressful. They often work long shifts, sometimes twelve hours without a proper rest.

Teachers do more than teach lessons. They prepare materials, check homework and help students with their problems. Many teachers say the best part of their job is seeing their students improve.

Some jobs are less visible. Cleaners keep our streets, offices and schools clean. Farmers grow the fruit and vegetables we buy in supermarkets. Delivery drivers bring parcels to our doors, even in rain and snow.

Next time you buy bread, take a bus or get a parcel, remember the people behind these services. A simple "thank you" can make their day better.

title: What People Wear Around the World
text:
Clothes are not only about fashion. In many countries, they also show history, culture and even the weather.

In Japan, the kimono is a traditional long robe with wide sleeves. Today, most Japanese people wear modern clothes, but they put on a kimono for special events like weddings and festivals.

In Scotland, some men wear a kilt, a knee-length skirt with a special pattern called tartan. Each family has its own tartan colours. Kilts are popular at weddings and sports events.

People in hot, dry places often wear long, loose clothes. This might sound strange, but loose cotton clothes protect the skin from the sun and keep the body cool. In many desert countries, men also cover their heads with a light scarf.

In very cold places like northern Canada, people wear thick coats, warm boots, hats and gloves. The Inuit people traditionally made warm clothes from animal skins.

Today, jeans and T-shirts are popular almost everywhere. However, traditional clothes are still important because they connect people with their past.

title: How Do People Travel?
text:
Two hundred years ago, most people walked or rode horses. A journey between two cities could take several days. Today, we can travel across the world in less than a day.

Cars are the most common way to travel in many countries. They are comfortable, and you can go wherever you want. However, cars cause traffic jams and air pollution, especially in big cities.

That is why many cities are improving public transport. In London, millions of people use the Underground every day. In Tokyo, trains are so punctual that a delay of one minute is unusual.

Bicycles are becoming popular again. In Amsterdam, there are more bikes than people! Cycling is cheap, healthy and good for the environment.

For long distances, people usually fly. Planes are fast, but flying is expensive and produces a lot of pollution. Some travellers now choose high-speed trains instead. In Europe, some trains can travel at 300 kilometres per hour.

Which way of travelling is the best? It depends on where you are going, how much money you have and how fast you need to get there.

title: Amazing Animals
text:
The animal world is full of surprises. Here are some facts that might amaze you.

Elephants have excellent memories. They can remember places where they found water many years before. They also seem to show feelings: when a member of the group dies, other elephants often stand next to the body for hours.

Octopuses are some of the smartest animals in the sea. They have eight arms and three hearts, and they can change the colour of their skin in less than a second. In aquariums, some octopuses have learned to open jars to get food.

The cheetah is the fastest land animal. It can run at about 110 kilometres per hour, but only for a short time. After a fast run, it needs to rest for up to half an hour.

Some birds travel incredible distances. The Arctic tern flies from the north of the planet to the south and back every year. During its life, it can fly about the same distance as three trips to the Moon and back.

Scientists are still discovering new species every year. Who knows what amazing animals we will find next?

title: Simple Habits for a Healthy Life
text:
You don't need an expensive gym or a special diet to be healthy. Small daily habits can make a big difference.

The first habit is drinking enough water. Our bodies are about sixty per cent water, and we lose some every day. Doctors usually recommend six to eight glasses a day. If you feel tired or have a headache, you might simply be thirsty.

The second habit is moving more. You don't have to run a marathon. Walking for thirty minutes a day, using the stairs instead of the lift or cycling to school is enough to keep your heart strong.

Sleep is the third important habit. Teenagers need eight to ten hours of sleep. Using your phone late at night makes it harder to fall asleep, so try to put it away an hour before bed.

Fourth, eat more fruit and vegetables and less sugar. Fast food is quick and tasty, but if you eat it every day, it can cause health problems.

Finally, take care of your mind. Spend time with friends, go outside and take short breaks when you study. A healthy life is a happy life.

title: How Technology Helps Us
text:
Think about your day. How many times do you use technology? For most of us, the answer is: all the time.

Technology helps us communicate. Fifty years ago, a letter to another country took weeks. Today, we can send a message or make a video call to anyone in the world in seconds. This is especially important for families who live far apart.

Technology also makes learning easier. Students can watch online lessons, use dictionaries on their phones and practise English with apps. If you don't understand something, you can find the answer on the internet in a few minutes.

In medicine, technology saves lives. Doctors use modern machines to find illnesses early. Some operations are now done with the help of robots, which are very precise.

Technology is useful at home too. Washing machines and dishwashers save us hours of housework every week, and maps on our phones help us find our way in a new city.

But technology has some disadvantages. Spending too many hours in front of screens can be bad for our eyes and our sleep. The key is to use technology wisely.

title: The Story Behind a Famous Movie
text:
In 1912, the Titanic was the biggest ship in the world. People said it could never sink. But on its first journey, from England to New York, it hit an iceberg in the Atlantic Ocean. More than 1,500 people died.

Eighty-five years later, the director James Cameron made a film about this tragedy. He was interested in the ship for many years. Before filming, he travelled to the bottom of the ocean in a small submarine and saw the real Titanic. He went down twelve times!

Making the film was not easy. The team built a huge copy of the ship in Mexico, almost as long as the real one. They also used a giant water tank to film the scenes when the ship sinks. The actors spent many hours in cold water.

The film was very expensive, and many people thought it would fail. But when it came out in 1997, millions of people went to cinemas to see the love story of Jack and Rose. The film won eleven Oscars and became one of the most successful films in history.

title: Four Seasons of the Year
text:
Why do we have seasons? Many people think it is because the Earth is closer to the Sun in summer. In fact, the reason is different. The Earth is tilted, so during the year, different parts of the planet get more or less sunlight.

In spring, the days get longer and warmer. Trees grow new leaves, flowers appear, and many birds return from warmer countries. Farmers start planting their crops.

Summer is the hottest season. The sun rises early and sets late, so we have long evenings. Schools close for the holidays, and many families go to the beach or the mountains.

In autumn, the weather becomes cooler, and leaves turn yellow, orange and red before they fall. Farmers harvest fruit and vegetables. Some animals, like squirrels, collect food for the winter.

Winter is the coldest season. In many places, it snows, and lakes freeze. Some animals, like bears, sleep for most of the winter.

Interestingly, when it is winter in the north of the planet, it is summer in the south. In Australia, people often celebrate the New Year on the beach!
